intended_object: The identification R ⧸ I ≃ R ⧸ J, as topological additive groups, coming from a proof that the ideals I and J are equal. This is read off the docstring and the body (`subst` followed by `ContinuousAddEquiv.refl`).
explanation:
This is a technical device: it moves a quotient along an equality of ideals. Mathematically it is just the identity of R ⧸ I, rewritten so that Lean will accept it as a map to R ⧸ J. The body substitutes J := I and returns `ContinuousAddEquiv.refl`. It is used inside the file at lines 211 and 234, together with its `_mk` simp lemma (`mk I x ↦ mk J x`), to rewrite between quotients whose ideals are only provably equal, not definitionally equal.

It has no counterpart in the literature beyond "R/I = R/J when I = J", so it does not define a mathematical object of its own. Mathlib has the same kind of device for rings, `Ideal.quotEquivOfEq`, which is a `RingEquiv`, but no topological additive version.

The commutativity assumption on R is not needed; any ring, or even any additive group with subgroups, would work. That is irrelevant, though, since this is a transport lemma and not a mathematical notion. Nothing in it is incorrect.
